subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Ultra-High-Performance Concrete
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Ultra-High-Performance Concrete.

hook.text: Normal concrete can handle 30 MPa of compression. Ultra-high-performance concrete handles 200 MPa.

buildup.text: UHPC uses fine powders, steel fibers, and minimal water. It's so dense that it's nearly waterproof.

discovery.text: Steel fibers replace rebar. They catch cracks at the micro level before they can spread.

twist.text: UHPC costs 5 to 10 times more than regular concrete. It's only used where extreme strength justifies the price.

climax.text: The Millau Viaduct's deck uses UHPC. Thinner sections saved enough weight to change the entire bridge design.

punchline.text: Seven times stronger. Ten times the price. Worth it.

quiz.question: What replaces traditional rebar in ultra-high-performance concrete?
options: Bamboo fibers that flex under heavy loads
Steel fibers mixed throughout that catch cracks at the micro level
Carbon nanotubes embedded during the curing process
